Its input schema declares no parameters, so do not assume it accepts a ticker or interval through the schema.

syn-market.company_filings.use_when: The user asks for recent regulatory filings (e.g. SEC-style reports) of a company. The tool takes no parameters, so it lists filings only from the server's default scope; use it when the user wants filings and no more specific tool or company identifier is required.
syn-market.company_filings.not_when: Do not use for a stock's current price (syn-market.get_quote), historical price candles (syn-market.get_ohlc), upcoming earnings dates (syn-market.earnings_calendar), or currency exchange rates (syn-market.fx_rate). It takes no company argument, so it cannot filter to a named company; for general web research about a company use syn-web.web_search instead.

syn-market.earnings_calendar.use_when: The user asks for upcoming earnings dates or which companies report earnings soon. Takes no arguments, so it returns the calendar as a whole; use it for broad 'what reports this week' style questions.
syn-market.earnings_calendar.not_when: Do not use for a single company's price (use syn-market.get_quote), historical candles (use syn-market.get_ohlc), or regulatory filings such as 10-Q or 8-K (use syn-market.company_filings). Earnings results or analyst estimates are not provided by any listed tool.

syn-market.fx_rate.use_when: The user asks for the current spot exchange rate between two currencies (e.g. EUR to USD, GBP/JPY). Input schema has no parameters, so the currency pair must be determined from the request before calling.
syn-market.fx_rate.not_when: Stock or equity prices for a ticker (use syn-market.get_quote). Historical or intraday candles (use syn-market.get_ohlc). Converting a specific amount of money for expenses or budgets (use syn-finance.currency_convert). Weather or general web questions about currencies (use syn-web.web_search).

syn-cloudops.list_instances.use_when: The user asks to see, list, or check compute instances (virtual machines or servers) and their current state or region, e.g. which instances are running or stopped, or where instances are deployed. Takes no inputs, so it can be called directly.
syn-cloudops.list_instances.not_when: Requests to restart an instance (syn-cloudops.restart_instance), to check spend (syn-cloudops.get_cost_report), to list storage buckets (syn-cloudops.list_buckets), to inspect an IAM role (syn-cloudops.describe_iam_role), or to deploy infrastructure (syn-cloudops.deploy_stack). Questions about how a cloud service works in general belong to documentation servers such as aws-knowledge, not this tool.

syn-cloudops.restart_instance.use_when: The user asks to restart, reboot or bounce a compute instance. The tool takes no parameters, so it can only act once the target instance is identified; if no instance is specified, list instances first with syn-cloudops.list_instances.
syn-cloudops.restart_instance.not_when: Requests to list or check instance state (syn-cloudops.list_instances), to deploy or update infrastructure (syn-cloudops.deploy_stack), to review spend (syn-cloudops.get_cost_report), or to restart a service or process inside an instance, which this tool does not describe. Questions about how restarts work in AWS docs belong to aws-knowledge.aws___read_documentation.

syn-cloudops.get_cost_report.use_when: The user asks for cloud spend, costs, or billing broken down by service for a period (e.g. 'what did we spend on cloud last month?'). Takes no inputs; the period is not a parameter, so use it for the overall cost-by-service view.
syn-cloudops.get_cost_report.not_when: Requests to list compute instances or their states (syn-cloudops.list_instances), to inspect IAM roles (syn-cloudops.describe_iam_role), or to view finance invoices and budgets (syn-finance.list_invoices, syn-finance.get_budget). Do not use for metrics or performance data (syn-monitoring.query_metrics), or for a specific date range or per-resource cost filtering, since this tool accepts no parameters.

syn-cloudops.list_buckets.use_when: The user asks to list, see, or check object storage buckets in the cloud account (e.g. S3-style buckets), or wants to find a bucket by name before doing something with it. No arguments are needed.
syn-cloudops.list_buckets.not_when: Requests about compute VMs or their state (syn-cloudops.list_instances), spend or billing (syn-cloudops.get_cost_report), IAM roles or policies (syn-cloudops.describe_iam_role), or file storage of user documents (syn-storage.list_folder, syn-storage.search_files). Do not use it to read or upload objects inside a bucket; it only lists buckets.

syn-cloudops.describe_iam_role.use_when: The user asks to describe, inspect, or review an IAM role and its attached policies in the cloud account. The tool takes no inputs, so it fits when a role context is already established.
syn-cloudops.describe_iam_role.not_when: Requests to list compute instances (syn-cloudops.list_instances), restart a server (syn-cloudops.restart_instance), check spend (syn-cloudops.get_cost_report), or list storage buckets (syn-cloudops.list_buckets). Questions about how IAM works in general, with no account role to inspect, belong to documentation tools such as aws-knowledge.aws___search_documentation.

syn-cloudops.deploy_stack.use_when: A user asks to deploy, apply or roll out an infrastructure-as-code stack (e.g. Terraform, CloudFormation or similar) to the cloud. It takes no input parameters, so the stack target is implied by the server context.
syn-cloudops.deploy_stack.not_when: Requests to restart a running compute instance (syn-cloudops.restart_instance), list instances or buckets, check spend (syn-cloudops.get_cost_report), inspect an IAM role (syn-cloudops.describe_iam_role), or find documentation or how-to guidance about IaC (aws-knowledge.aws___search_documentation, microsoft-learn.microsoft_docs_search).

syn-notes.create_note.use_when: The user wants to start a brand-new personal note with content they supply, and no existing note id or title is being targeted. Use this when the request is to write, jot down, or save something as a new note.
syn-notes.create_note.not_when: Do not use for adding text to an existing note (syn-notes.append_to_note). Do not use to find or read existing notes (syn-notes.search_notes). Do not use to create a wiki page or document (syn-wiki.create_page), a ticket (syn-tickets.create_issue), or a file (syn-storage.upload_file). Note: this tool's schema declares no input parameters, so it may need the content supplied through other means.

syn-notes.search_notes.use_when: The user wants to find or look up their own personal notes by a text query or keyword. Use this first when the user asks what they wrote or noted about something, before reading or changing any note. The tool takes no input parameters in its schema, so the query has to be supplied through the search itself.
syn-notes.search_notes.not_when: Requests to create a new note (syn-notes.create_note), add text to an existing note (syn-notes.append_to_note), or search workplace wiki pages (syn-wiki.search_pages), chat messages (syn-chat.search_messages), files (syn-storage.search_files) or email (syn-mail.search_mail). Also not for general web or documentation searches.

syn-notes.append_to_note.use_when: The user wants to add text to the end of an existing personal note and the target note is already identified. Use after syn-notes.search_notes if the note id is unknown. The input schema has no declared parameters, so supply the note reference and text as the tool expects.
syn-notes.append_to_note.not_when: Creating a brand-new note (syn-notes.create_note). Finding or locating a note by its content (syn-notes.search_notes). Editing or replacing existing note text rather than appending (no listed tool does this). Adding comments to a ticket (syn-tickets.add_comment) or wiki pages (syn-wiki.create_page) rather than personal notes.

syn-weather.current_weather.use_when: The user asks for the current weather conditions (right now, today's temperature, whether it is raining or sunny) in a city. The city name is the only thing needed, and the tool takes no parameters, so the location must be stated in the conversation or the request.
syn-weather.current_weather.not_when: Requests for weather over several days or future dates belong to syn-weather.forecast. Requests about a coordinate, address, or place lookup belong to syn-maps.geocode or syn-maps.search_places. Weather-related documentation or API questions are not served by this tool.

syn-weather.forecast.use_when: The user asks for a multi-day or upcoming-days weather forecast for a location (e.g. this week, the weekend, next few days). The input schema takes no parameters, so the location must be inferred from the request or established before calling.
syn-weather.forecast.not_when: Requests for the weather right now or current conditions in a city (use syn-weather.current_weather). Requests for travel-date weather planning that also involve booking (use syn-travel.search_flights or syn-travel.search_hotels). Requests for climate history, general weather science, or documentation questions, which no listed tool serves.

syn-maps.search_places.use_when: The user wants to find places or businesses by a query, such as restaurants, cafes, pharmacies or shops, near a location. Use it when the user names a place type or business and an area, even if only a city or neighbourhood name is given.
syn-maps.search_places.not_when: Do not use for turning a street address into coordinates (syn-maps.geocode), for route or travel-time directions between points (syn-maps.directions), or for flight, hotel or travel bookings (syn-travel.search_hotels, syn-travel.search_flights). Do not use for general web facts about places (syn-web.web_search).

syn-maps.directions.use_when: The user asks how to get from one place to another by driving, walking or public transit, and wants a route or travel directions. The input schema has no parameters, so origin and destination must be supplied through the agent's own context when the tool is invoked.
syn-maps.directions.not_when: Requests to find or look up places or businesses near a location (syn-maps.search_places), to convert an address into coordinates (syn-maps.geocode), or to plan flights or hotel travel (syn-travel.search_flights, syn-travel.search_hotels). Questions about live traffic or weather are not route requests.

syn-maps.geocode.use_when: The user wants to turn a street address, place name or postal address into latitude and longitude coordinates. Use it first when a later step needs coordinates and the user has supplied an address rather than coordinates.
syn-maps.geocode.not_when: Requests to find nearby places or businesses by category (syn-maps.search_places), routes or travel times between points (syn-maps.directions), or an address already given as coordinates. Requests for weather at a location (syn-weather.current_weather) or flight searches are not geocoding. Input schema has no parameters, so the address must be supplied by the agent in the call.

syn-ml-registry.search_models.use_when: The user wants to find or look up registered ML models by name, task type, or owner, or needs to discover a model's identifier before other registry actions. Use as the first call when the model is not yet identified.
syn-ml-registry.search_models.not_when: The user already has a model identifier and version and wants its metrics or artifacts (use syn-ml-registry.get_model_version). Requests to move a version to staging or production (use syn-ml-registry.promote_model). Requests about experiment runs or training metrics (use syn-ml-registry.list_experiments). Questions about public Hugging Face models (use huggingface.hub_repo_search). Generic web or code searches are not registry lookups.

syn-ml-registry.get_model_version.use_when: A user asks for metrics or artifacts of a specific model version and the version is already identified. The tool takes no parameters, so it can only be called when the server context fixes the version. Call search_models first if the model or version is not yet known.
syn-ml-registry.get_model_version.not_when: Requests to find models by name, task or owner (syn-ml-registry.search_models). Requests to promote a version to staging or production (syn-ml-registry.promote_model). Requests for experiment run metrics across runs (syn-ml-registry.list_experiments). Requests for live service metrics or dashboards (syn-monitoring.query_metrics). Requests for general ML documentation (huggingface.hub_repo_details or deepwiki).

syn-ml-registry.promote_model.use_when: A user asks to promote a specific registered model version to staging or production. The target stage and model version should be known before calling. Typically preceded by get_model_version to confirm metrics.
syn-ml-registry.promote_model.not_when: Looking up or finding models (search_models), inspecting a version's metrics or artifacts (get_model_version), or reviewing experiment runs (list_experiments). Requests to deploy infrastructure or stacks belong to syn-cloudops.deploy_stack. Requests to promote with no known model version should first use search_models or get_model_version.

syn-ml-registry.list_experiments.use_when: The user wants to see, compare or review experiment runs and their metrics (e.g. accuracy, loss across runs) without naming a specific model. Takes no arguments, so it lists runs broadly.
syn-ml-registry.list_experiments.not_when: Requests for metrics or artifacts of one known model version (use syn-ml-registry.get_model_version); finding registered models by name, task or owner (use syn-ml-registry.search_models); promoting a model to staging or production (use syn-ml-registry.promote_model); querying warehouse data or production monitoring metrics (use syn-warehouse.run_sql or syn-monitoring.query_metrics). Cannot filter by model or date since it takes no inputs.
